title: Diagnose a failed delivery pipeline action / Diagnose workload health failure from telemetry

steps.title: Diagnose a failed delivery pipeline action

blocks.text: Execution and action history identify failures and error details. Start with the first failing action in the selected execution; inspect its input revision and linked service logs to identify the correction.
After the approved correction, retest and verify that action succeeds before investigating later dependent actions that did not run.

nodes.label: Selected execution and input artifact revision
First failing build: error details and linked logs

blocks.alt_text: Show the selected CodePipeline execution with a successful source action, a failed build action and a deployment action that did not run. Make the failed action's input artifact revision, error details and linked service logs visible, followed by its successful retest with the intended input.

blocks.text: The supplied source succeeded, the build failed and deployment did not run. Inspect build error details and linked logs, apply the evidence-supported approved correction, then verify build success with the intended input. An unrun deployment is not an independent error.

steps.title: Review pipeline failure evidence
steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which conclusions or actions are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: After an approved correction to the first failed action, what should be verified before investigating later actions that did not run?

options.text: Retest and verify the corrected action succeeds with the intended input.
Investigate the skipped deployment first without retesting the failed action.
Treat approval of the correction as proof the action now succeeds.

a.message: Correct. Retest and verify the corrected action succeeds with the intended input.

b.message: Verify the corrected failure before investigating later dependent actions that did not run.

c.message: Approval does not replace execution evidence from the retest.

correct.message: Correct. Your judgement follows the supplied evidence and the stated requirement.

incorrect.message: Compare the evidence with the requirement rather than inferring success from a partial signal. Identify the first failing action in the selected execution, retain its execution and input revision identities, and select the approved correction supported by its error details and linked service logs. After the correction, verify that action succeeds with the intended input before investigating later dependent actions that did not run.

hints: Separate the observed outcome from what was merely intended.
Check every required condition, not just the most reassuring field.

public.prompt: Read selected execution/action evidence and the retest. Identify the first failed action with its supported correction, distinguish skipped dependencies, and judge verification of the corrected action with the intended input.

buckets.label: Later dependent action did not run
Corrected action verified with intended input

items.text:
For the original selected execution the action order is source, build, deployment. The correction shown was approved before retest; execution and input revision identities are retained. Retest success precedes investigation of later dependencies.
```text
execution_id: "pipeline-original"
revision: "exercise-revision"
action: "source"
status: "success"
error_details: ""
linked_service_logs: ""
approved_correction: ""
```

For the original selected execution the action order is source, build, deployment. The correction shown was approved before retest; execution and input revision identities are retained. Retest success precedes investigation of later dependencies.
```text
execution_id: "pipeline-original"
revision: "exercise-revision"
action: "build"
status: "failed"
error_details: "Build failed because the configured application directory was absent"
linked_service_logs: "Build log: cannot enter /workspace/app-old; supplied checkout contains /workspace/app"
approved_correction: "Change the build working directory to /workspace/app"
```

steps.title: Diagnose workload health failure from telemetry

blocks.text: EC2 system status checks concern underlying AWS host issues; instance checks concern instance software and networking.
Locate the affected workload using the supplied metric/log window. Inspect component service status, events and logs: the symptom alone does not prove its cause.
For a container, inspect state, exit status and recent logs. Apply the evidence-supported correction and repeat the supplied health check.

nodes.label: Component state, exit status and recent logs

blocks.alt_text: Show the supplied telemetry interval and affected workload alongside component inspection results, including container state, exit status and recent logs, with the original and repeated health-check results visible.

blocks.text: A restarted component or improved metric does not erase a failed health check. Tie component logs to the affected workload and telemetry interval, and retain original and repeated health-check outcomes after the approved correction.

steps.title: Review component health evidence
steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which conclusions or actions are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: Which pairing correctly distinguishes EC2 status-check boundaries?

options.text: System checks concern the underlying AWS host; instance checks concern instance software and networking.
System checks concern instance software; instance checks concern the underlying AWS host.
Both checks exclusively concern the underlying host.

a.message: Correct. System checks concern the underlying AWS host; instance checks concern instance software and networking.

b.message: These boundaries are reversed: system is host, instance is software and networking.

c.message: Instance checks cover the instance software and networking, not exclusively the underlying host.

correct.message: Correct. Your judgement follows the supplied evidence and the stated requirement.

incorrect.message: Compare the evidence with the requirement rather than inferring success from a partial signal. The affected workload and failing component are correctly identified from evidence within the supplied time window. The learner applies the evidence-supported approved correction and repeats the supplied health check, confirming that the original failure is resolved rather than relying only on an improved metric or restarted process.

hints: Separate the observed outcome from what was merely intended.
Check every required condition, not just the most reassuring field.

steps.title: Review component health evidence
steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which conclusions or actions are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: Read the time-correlated workload/component evidence. Decide whether each excerpt identifies the failure, shows an insufficient improvement, or verifies resolution through the repeated supplied health check.

buckets.label: Correlated component failure and supported correction
Improvement is not resolution: health check still fails
Correction verified by repeated supplied health check

items.text:
Service status and events were inspected for the shown affected workload and component in the supplied time window. Container state, exit status and recent logs were inspected. The supplied approved correction is supported by the original component log; the original and repeated health-check results remain visible.
```text
workload: "exercise-container"
interval_start: "2026-01-15T10:00:00+00:00"
interval_end: "2026-01-15T10:05:00+00:00"
component: "application container"
telemetry: "Client request health checks fail"
container_state: "exited"
exit_status: 1
recent_logs: "Supplied log identifies a component configuration error"
health_check: "fail"
correction: "Supplied approved component configuration correction"
```

where.recent_logs: Supplied log identifies a component configuration error
